facts.raw_span: A 40-year-old woman presented with abdominal pain and constipation
continued to have amenorrhea and reported abdominal fullness and constipation
Point-of-care (POC) urine human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) test: negative
Ultrasonography: Confirmed live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks

continued to have amenorrhea and reported abdominal fullness and constipation
Point-of-care (POC) urine human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) test: negative
Ultrasonography: Confirmed live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks

concepts.why: The patient presented with amenorrhea and a high serum hCG level, and ultrasonography confirmed a live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks.
The patient had a history of thyroid condition, and thyroid-stimulating hormone was undetectable, leading to a prescription of methimazole.
The patient presented with constipation and abdominal fullness.
The patient had a tender midline abdominal mass on physical examination.
The patient's constipation may be related to her pregnancy.
The patient's abdominal mass may be related to her pregnancy.
It explains the initially negative point-of-care urine human chorionic gonadotropin test despite a confirmed pregnancy.

rationales.F01: Abdominal pain and constipation could be related to various conditions, including constipation or abdominal mass, but are not specific enough to rule in or out any concept strongly.
rationales.F02: Amenorrhea can be related to pregnancy or other conditions such as hyperthyroidism, but in the context of other symptoms, it leans towards pregnancy-related conditions.
rationales.F04: Undetectable thyroid-stimulating hormone suggests hyperthyroidism, which is supported by the prescription of methimazole.
rationales.F08: A tender midline abdominal mass could be related to several conditions, including pregnancy or an abdominal mass, but the presence of this symptom alongside others helps to rule in pregnancy-related conditions.
rationales.F09: A negative point-of-care urine hCG test could suggest that the test was a false negative, especially given the high serum hCG levels found later.
rationales.F10: High serum hCG levels are strongly indicative of pregnancy, making this finding crucial for ruling in intrauterine pregnancy.
rationales.F11: Ultrasonography confirming a live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks is definitive evidence for intrauterine pregnancy and rules out other conditions.
